EL5-F-01.hint: Quotient rule first (a quotient becomes a difference), then the product rule (a product becomes a sum), then bring each exponent down in front with the power rule.
slips: Distributing the log over a sum, as in \(\log(a+b)=\log a+\log b\). That is not a property.
Forgetting parentheses when the denominator has two factors; both are subtracted.

EL5-F-02.hint: Move each coefficient into an exponent first (the power rule backward). Then add logs by multiplying and subtract logs by dividing.
slips: Putting the coefficient in front of the argument instead of as its exponent.
Multiplying the subtracted term instead of dividing by it.

EL5-A-01.hint: Factor the number into the numbers you are given logs for. Products become sums, quotients become differences, and exponents come down in front.
slips: Writing \(\log_b(12)\) as \(\log_b(3)\cdot\log_b(4)\). A product inside becomes a sum outside.
Treating a square root as \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) times the number instead of the exponent \(\dfrac{1}{2}\).

EL5-A-02.hint: Combine into a single logarithm first, then ask what power of the base gives the result.
slips: Adding the arguments when the logs are added. A sum of logs is the log of a product.
Subtracting the arguments when the logs are subtracted. A difference of logs is the log of a quotient.

parts.q: Expand \(\log_{6}\left(\dfrac{xy^{2}}{z^{3}}\right)\), showing the property used at each step.
parts.a: Quotient rule: \(\log_{6}\left(xy^{2}\right) - \log_{6}\left(z^{3}\right)\). Product rule: \(\log_{6}\left(x\right) + \log_{6}\left(y^{2}\right) - \log_{6}\left(z^{3}\right)\). Power rule: \(\log_{6} x + 2\log_{6} y - 3\log_{6} z\).

parts.q: Expand \(\log_{3}\left(\dfrac{m^{2}n}{p^{2}}\right)\), showing the property used at each step.
parts.a: Quotient rule: \(\log_{3}\left(m^{2}n\right) - \log_{3}\left(p^{2}\right)\). Product rule: \(\log_{3}\left(m^{2}\right) + \log_{3}\left(n\right) - \log_{3}\left(p^{2}\right)\). Power rule: \(2\log_{3} m + \log_{3} n - 2\log_{3} p\).

parts.q: Expand \(\log_{4}\left(\dfrac{uv}{w^{2}k}\right)\), showing the property used at each step.
parts.a: Quotient rule: \(\log_{4}\left(uv\right) - \log_{4}\left(w^{2}k\right)\). Product rule: \(\log_{4}\left(u\right) + \log_{4}\left(v\right) - \left(\log_{4}\left(w^{2}\right) + \log_{4}\left(k\right)\right)\). Power rule: \(\log_{4} u + \log_{4} v - 2\log_{4} w - \log_{4} k\).

parts.q: Expand \(\ln\left(\dfrac{m^{3}n}{p}\right)\), showing the property used at each step.
parts.a: Quotient rule: \(\ln\left(m^{3}n\right) - \ln\left(p\right)\). Product rule: \(\ln\left(m^{3}\right) + \ln\left(n\right) - \ln\left(p\right)\). Power rule: \(3\ln m + \ln n - \ln p\).

parts.q: Expand \(\log_{4}\left(\dfrac{x^{3}y}{z^{2}}\right)\), showing the property used at each step.
parts.a: Quotient rule: \(\log_{4}\left(x^{3}y\right) - \log_{4}\left(z^{2}\right)\). Product rule: \(\log_{4}\left(x^{3}\right) + \log_{4}\left(y\right) - \log_{4}\left(z^{2}\right)\). Power rule: \(3\log_{4} x + \log_{4} y - 2\log_{4} z\).

parts.q: Expand \(\log_{6}\left(\dfrac{m^{3}n}{p^{2}s}\right)\), showing the property used at each step.
parts.a: Quotient rule: \(\log_{6}\left(m^{3}n\right) - \log_{6}\left(p^{2}s\right)\). Product rule: \(\log_{6}\left(m^{3}\right) + \log_{6}\left(n\right) - \left(\log_{6}\left(p^{2}\right) + \log_{6}\left(s\right)\right)\). Power rule: \(3\log_{6} m + \log_{6} n - 2\log_{6} p - \log_{6} s\).

parts.q: Expand \(\log_{6}\left(\dfrac{x^{3}y}{z^{2}}\right)\), showing the property used at each step.
parts.a: Quotient rule: \(\log_{6}\left(x^{3}y\right) - \log_{6}\left(z^{2}\right)\). Product rule: \(\log_{6}\left(x^{3}\right) + \log_{6}\left(y\right) - \log_{6}\left(z^{2}\right)\). Power rule: \(3\log_{6} x + \log_{6} y - 2\log_{6} z\).

parts.q: Expand \(\ln\left(\dfrac{x^{2}y}{z}\right)\), showing the property used at each step.
parts.a: Quotient rule: \(\ln\left(x^{2}y\right) - \ln\left(z\right)\). Product rule: \(\ln\left(x^{2}\right) + \ln\left(y\right) - \ln\left(z\right)\). Power rule: \(2\ln x + \ln y - \ln z\).

parts.q: Expand \(\log_{7}\left(\dfrac{a^{3}b}{c^{3}s^{2}}\right)\), showing the property used at each step.
parts.a: Quotient rule: \(\log_{7}\left(a^{3}b\right) - \log_{7}\left(c^{3}s^{2}\right)\). Product rule: \(\log_{7}\left(a^{3}\right) + \log_{7}\left(b\right) - \left(\log_{7}\left(c^{3}\right) + \log_{7}\left(s^{2}\right)\right)\). Power rule: \(3\log_{7} a + \log_{7} b - 3\log_{7} c - 2\log_{7} s\).

parts.q: Expand \(\log_{2}\left(\dfrac{a^{2}b^{2}}{c^{3}}\right)\), showing the property used at each step.
parts.a: Quotient rule: \(\log_{2}\left(a^{2}b^{2}\right) - \log_{2}\left(c^{3}\right)\). Product rule: \(\log_{2}\left(a^{2}\right) + \log_{2}\left(b^{2}\right) - \log_{2}\left(c^{3}\right)\). Power rule: \(2\log_{2} a + 2\log_{2} b - 3\log_{2} c\).

parts.q: Expand \(\log_{7}\left(\dfrac{uv^{2}}{w}\right)\), showing the property used at each step.
parts.a: Quotient rule: \(\log_{7}\left(uv^{2}\right) - \log_{7}\left(w\right)\). Product rule: \(\log_{7}\left(u\right) + \log_{7}\left(v^{2}\right) - \log_{7}\left(w\right)\). Power rule: \(\log_{7} u + 2\log_{7} v - \log_{7} w\).

parts.q: Expand \(\log_{2}\left(\dfrac{m^{3}n^{2}}{p^{3}s^{2}}\right)\), showing the property used at each step.
parts.a: Quotient rule: \(\log_{2}\left(m^{3}n^{2}\right) - \log_{2}\left(p^{3}s^{2}\right)\). Product rule: \(\log_{2}\left(m^{3}\right) + \log_{2}\left(n^{2}\right) - \left(\log_{2}\left(p^{3}\right) + \log_{2}\left(s^{2}\right)\right)\). Power rule: \(3\log_{2} m + 2\log_{2} n - 3\log_{2} p - 2\log_{2} s\).
